questions.question: Differentiate in detail between training and pruning in horticultural crops.
questions.solution_html:
• Training
  • Training refers to the judicious removal of plant part / parts to develop proper shape
  • of a plant capable of bearing a heavy crop load.
  • (i) Open centre system (Vase shaped) In this system the main stem is allowed to
  • grow to a certain height and the leader is cut to encourage lateral scaffold from near
  • the ground giving a vase shaped plant. This is common in peaches, apricots
  • (ii) Central leader system (closed centre) In this system the central axis of plant is
  • allowed to grow unhindered permitting branches all around. This system is also
  • known as closed centre system and common in use in apple, pear, mango and sapota.
  • (iii) Modified leader system This system is in between open centre and central leader
  • system wherein central axis is allowed to grow unhindered upto 4—5 years and then
  • the central stem is headed back and laterals are permitted .It is common in apple, pear
  • cherry, plum, and guava
  • Pruning
  • Pruning is the removal of unwanted, surplus annual growth; dead, dried and diseased
  • wood of the plants is called Pruning.
  • i. Thinning out:When a shoot is entirely removed from the point of its origin and no
  • re-growth is allowed to occur from the cut ends.
  • ii. Heading back:When the terminal portion of branch/shoot is removed and it
  • encourages lateral growth from the remaining shoot.
  • iii. Notching:Removal of wedge shaped bark piece from above the bud to make a
  • notch is called as notching.
  • iv. Nicking:Removal of wedge shaped bark piece below the bud to make a notch is
  • called as notching.
  • Sufficient availability of manure at a cheap rate in the locality.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: Sufficient availability of manure at a cheap rate in the locality.

questions.question: Briefly describe about lath house,net house and mist house.
questions.solution_html:
• Briefly describe about lath house,net house and mist house.
  • Lath house-it is a valuable asset in raising seedling,rooted cuttings and young plants
  • prior to setting them out in the garden. Lath house will modify the environment in
  • which they are growing by offering protection from hot,drying summer
  • winds,reducing the intensity of sunlight,lowering temperature and maintaining higher
  • humidity.
  • Mist house-it is a technique for minimising plant moisture loss by controlled
  • periodic wetting of the foliage of cuttings which are being rooted. It is helpful for
  • rooting leafy cuttings.
  • Net house-net houses are widely used as propagation structures in tropical
  • areas,where artificial heating is not required and artificial cooling is expensive. Net
  • houses may be constructed with roofs covered with glass or plastic film and its sides
  • are covered with wire net. It maintains ideal temperature for germination of seeds.
  • Availability of skilled labour plentily and at a cheap rate in the locality of the
  • orchard.

questions.question: Dicuss in detail about propagation by budding.
questions.solution_html:
• The plant that grows after union of the stock and the bud is known as budding.
  •  T-budding-the cuts given on the stock are of the shape of the letter T. It is widely
  • used for propagating fruit trees and many ornamental plants. Eg;rose and citrus
  •  Inverted T budding-inverted T budding procedure is same as that of T budding
  • except the horizontal cut on the stock is made at the bottom of the vertical cut
  • rather than at the top.
  •  Patch budding-a regular patch of bark is completely removed from the stock
  • plant and is replaced with a patch of bark of the same size containing a bud from
  • the desired mother plant.Eg;walnut
  •  Ring budding-in the root stock,two transverse cut 1.5 cm apart are made and
  • these are connected with a vertical cut and a ring of bark is removed.
  •  Flute budding-in flute budding,the patch of bark is removed from the stock is
  • such a way that it completely encircles the stock except with a narrow bark
  • connection between the upper and lower cuts on the stock.
  •  Forkert budding-the stock is prepared by giving two vertical cuts and a
  • transverse cuts above the vertical cuts to join them. The bark is removed carefully
  • along the cuts,so the flap of bark hangs down. The scion is then slipped into the
  • exposed portion of the stock and the flap is drawn over the inserted bud patch. It
  • is then tied with a wrapping material.
  •  Chip budding-a chip is removed from the budwood, ensuring that the bud is in
  • the middle of the chip. The chip bud is then inserted in the stock in such a way
  • that cambium of the bud chip should have direct contact with the cambium of the
  • stock.
